newsitem.title: UK: LME copper stays clear of lows in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper stays clear of lows in late London.

text.p: LME copper held on during late inter-office activity to gains that it had made in a rebound from Wednesday's drop down near the psychological $2,300 per tonne level.
Successive waves of selling, largely fund liquidation, had pressured three month copper prices, which bottomed out at $2,305 before a bounce on short-covering and trade buying.
The market finished the kerb with pared losses of $8 at $2,325 and was bid at $2,324 by the time Comex closed at 1900 GMT.
Nickel joined copper in a modest rally, bouncing off a low of $7,870 to finish the day back above the 30-day moving average and around the $8,000 mark. It was bid at $7,990 by 1900 GMT.

Nickel prices have already gained some 30 percent since the end of 1996 and further advances are expected for the rest of this year and in 1998, Dr Mo Ahmadzadeh president of Rudolf Wolff and Co Inc said.
In a speech prepared for delivery at the Institute of Scrap Re-cycling Industries (ISRI) annual convention in Las Vegas, Ahmadzadeh said the market may pull back in the short term to around $7,500.

Aluminium also got a minor boost from copper's rebound, prying itself loose of the $1,640 level it had held most of the day to close the kerb at its high of $1,647, a gain of $5. It held these values in late activity. -London Newsroom +44 v171 542 7729
